mechanisms.title: Item Category Determination
mechanisms.memory_hook: The item category is the item's operating license.
mechanisms.question: What is this sales item allowed to do?

inputs.name: item usage
inputs.origin: process context; sometimes set internally by SAP

mechanisms.determination: Item category determination is a Customizing lookup. SAP evaluates sales document type + material item category group + item usage + higher-level item category. The matching assignment proposes a default item category and can also define allowed alternative item categories that the user may select. Usage is often blank for normal material items; SAP can set TEXT internally for text items entered without a material in inquiries or quotations, and FREE for free-goods items.
configuration_surfaces: Assign Item Categories: sales document type + item category group + usage + higher-level item category
Maintain the default item category and any allowed manual alternatives
Standard examples to recognize: TAN standard, TATX text, TANN free of charge, TAS third-party; customer configuration can use different categories

failure_modes.prove: Trace sales document type + item category group + usage + higher-level item category, then check the matching default category before changing configuration.

failure_modes.symptom: Expected alternative item category cannot be selected
failure_modes.prove: Check whether that alternative is explicitly allowed for the same determination combination; a category can exist without being selectable here.

failure_modes.symptom: Text or free-goods item gets unexpected behavior
failure_modes.prove: Prove the usage value first. TEXT and FREE can steer item-category determination before downstream pricing, schedule-line or billing checks.

failure_modes.symptom: No schedule line or wrong billing behavior
failure_modes.prove: Prove the item category first; those symptoms may be downstream effects rather than separate defects.

failure_modes.symptom: Special item behaves like a normal item
failure_modes.prove: Trace item category group, usage and higher-level item category. For BOMs, first prove whether ERLA or LUMF is intended.

tests.setup: Keep the sales document type constant and change only the material item-category group.
tests.assert: The proposed item category follows the maintained determination combination.

tests.setup: Maintain one default item category and one allowed alternative for the same determination key.
tests.assert: SAP proposes the default category and the configured alternative is available for manual selection.

tests.setup: Create a subitem under a known higher-level item category.
tests.assert: The higher-level item category participates in item-category determination.

tests.setup: Compare a normal material item with a supported text-item or free-goods scenario.
tests.assert: The usage context participates in determination and leads to the configured item-category behavior.

tests.setup: Create a normal item, a text item, a free-of-charge subitem and a Sales BOM in controlled standard-like configuration.
tests.assert: Each item receives the expected category and different pricing, schedule-line, delivery or subitem behavior.

item_examples.note: Classic standard example. A text item can be used without a material number and is controlled separately from a normal material item.
Classic standard example for a free-of-charge item; free-goods determination can create it as a subitem.
Classic third-party example: the item category participates in switching fulfillment from own delivery to procurement.
Common standard Sales BOM categories associated with ERLA and LUMF processing; always read them together with item category group and higher-level item context.
Standard delivery item example for make-to-order production from a standard order.

mechanisms.title: Partner Determination
mechanisms.memory_hook: A document is not just what was sold; it is who is allowed to play each role.
mechanisms.question: Who is sold-to, ship-to, bill-to, payer, contact, or another process partner, and why?
mechanisms.determination: A partner determination procedure defines the partner functions, whether they are mandatory or changeable, and how partners are sourced.
outputs: partner functions at header and/or item level
configuration_surfaces: Assign procedures to document types and item categories

failure_modes.prove: Check procedure assignment, mandatory functions, source control, and master partner relationships.
Compare the actual partner functions before debugging the downstream mechanism.

tests.setup: Use a sold-to with a distinct ship-to and payer relationship.
tests.assert: Document partner functions are populated according to the assigned procedure and source rules.

mechanisms.title: Pricing
mechanisms.memory_hook: First prove the procedure. Only then hunt the condition record.
mechanisms.question: Which pricing procedure runs, and how does it find each price element?
mechanisms.determination: Sales area + customer pricing procedure + document pricing procedure determine the pricing procedure. The procedure then processes condition types and their access sequences to find condition records.

failure_modes.symptom: Condition record exists but price is missing
failure_modes.prove: Prove pricing procedure → condition type → access sequence → access key → validity before editing the record.
Check copy-control pricing type and whether billing reprices or copies conditions.

tests.setup: Create two customers with different customer pricing procedure values and identical material/quantity.
tests.assert: The determined pricing procedure follows the configured key.

tests.setup: Maintain a specific customer-material condition and a generic fallback.
tests.assert: The access sequence finds the more specific valid record first when configured that way.

mechanisms.title: Copy Control
mechanisms.memory_hook: A follow-on document inherits rules, not just fields.
mechanisms.question: What is allowed to flow from source to target, and what is redetermined?

inputs.name: copying requirements / data transfer / quantity / pricing type

mechanisms.determination: Copy-control settings at header/item level decide whether reference creation is allowed and how data, quantities, status and pricing move into the target.

failure_modes.prove: Check source/target pair → item category entry → copying requirement → status and completion rule.

failure_modes.symptom: Wrong price or quantity in target
failure_modes.prove: Check item-level pricing type, quantity rule and data-transfer routine before blaming pricing itself.

tests.setup: Create a quotation then create an order with reference.
tests.assert: Expected quantities, references, statuses and configured pricing behavior are transferred.

tests.setup: Change pricing type between copy and repricing behavior in a controlled test configuration.
tests.assert: Target pricing changes exactly at the copy-control boundary.

mechanisms.title: Incompletion Procedure and Log
mechanisms.memory_hook: Completeness is a process control, not a cosmetic warning.
mechanisms.question: Which missing fields make this document incomplete, and what may be blocked because of them?

inputs.name: sales document type / item category / schedule-line context
fields and status groups defined for the procedure
actual document data and missing values

mechanisms.determination: The incompletion procedure defines which fields are checked for the relevant sales-document context and how missing data affects status. The incompletion log records missing data; depending on configuration and the missing field, further processing such as copying, delivery or billing can be blocked even when the document itself can be saved.
configuration_surfaces: Assign incompletion procedures to sales document types and item categories
Define fields and status groups relevant for further processing

failure_modes.symptom: Order saves but delivery or billing is blocked
failure_modes.prove: Open the incompletion log and identify the missing field → status group → affected follow-on function before changing copy, delivery or billing configuration.

failure_modes.symptom: Business expects a mandatory field but SAP does not flag it
failure_modes.prove: Check the procedure assignment and whether the field is included in the relevant incompletion procedure for the correct header/item/schedule-line context.

failure_modes.symptom: A harmless missing field blocks too much processing
failure_modes.prove: Trace the field's status-group effect before removing the field from completeness control entirely.

tests.setup: Create a sales document with one configured required field missing and inspect the incompletion log and document status.
tests.assert: The missing field appears in the log and the configured follow-on processing effect is visible.

tests.setup: Compare two missing fields assigned to different status effects in a controlled test design.
tests.assert: Only the follow-on functions configured for each incompleteness case are blocked.
